The Minutes go to everyone on the Project Charter's stakeholder list, not only to the 21 who turned up — which is 81 email addresses. Florence insists, because half her division learns what is happening from documents they are copied into.

a: Six actions, six owners, six dates
d: What the kick-off minutes actually commit anybody to. An action without a named owner and a date is not an action. Four of the six are the Project Manager's; taking the 81 addresses makes it five.

The Project Handbook, printed because Florence does not read long documents on screen. It describes how the project is run — approach, controlling processes, rules, escalation route, who holds which role — not what gets built. What gets built is the Charter, and later the Work Plan.

The three things that must be true or CASTOR fails: Lending Operations releases its people for the whole build; Florence is visibly the owner; and SC1 to SC5 are still measurable in 2028. The first is a promise about her staffing, not about the project, which is exactly why it is on page one.

a: six management plans and four documents
d: The tailoring decision: CASTOR needs six management plans, but only four of them are separate documents. Requirements, issue, quality and communications each get their own; risk and change stay as sections 4.1 and 4.4 of the Handbook, because a whole plan would only ever be read by the Project Manager.

The Project Stakeholder Matrix has 22 rows grouped as teams, roles, support, operational and one catch-all group at the bottom. It is not finished: Florence can name six more people in Finance and Control, three of whom will be reconciling this system at seven in the morning.

a: six people in Finance and Control
d: The gap Florence spots in the stakeholder matrix: six people in Finance and Control who are not on it, three of whom will be reconciling the new system early every morning. Missing a stakeholder is how you find out about them at acceptance instead of at planning.

Why Lorenzo de' Medici is 'medium interest' even though he chairs the board that funded CASTOR: he has eleven other projects and about forty minutes a year for this one. That combination decides what to send him and how often — which is where the communications plan starts.

The Project Steering Committee has four permanent members: Project Owner, Solution Provider, Business Manager and Project Manager. Everyone else — quality assurance, the user representative, the architecture office — is there because the project needs them, and some advise without voting.

What independent quality assurance found when Deming checked the Charter against the Business Case: the reconciliation target in section 3.2 had drifted to 'next day', and the risk table had no owners. Both fixed before the meeting. This is why the author does not review their own document.

There are only three credible vendors in this market, and Florence can name all three from memory. That is why she wants to skip to a tender — and why the Business Case still has to compare options rather than suppliers.

Marie Curie's team: the 40 people who do the typing today and whose working day the new platform rewrites. Retraining them is deliverable D-04, work package 1.7, and it belongs in Grace's Business Implementation Plan — not in the Project Manager's Transition Plan.

The small ESM meeting room where most of the early CASTOR meetings happen: eight seats, one screen that gives everybody a green cast, and a video kit nobody trusts. The Initiating Meeting (9 Jan 2026), the first Steering Committee (10 Mar), the Charter signing (24 Mar) and the RfP gate review (27 Mar) are all held here.

The good room: a working screen, working microphones and a table for twenty-two. It is where the Corporate Investment Board meets, chaired by Lorenzo de' Medici. Getting an item on this agenda is how CASTOR gets money.

Lending Operations lives on the fourth floor of the ESM's Kirchberg building, and so does the windowless file room used as the project room. IT and Digital (Leonardo's division) is two floors below; the Project Support Office is on the third floor; the big meeting rooms are B4-12, A1-02 and B-2.04.

a: the camera that has pointed at the ceiling tiles
d: Room B-2.04 is the long meeting room used for the Planning Kick-off and most Steering Committees from April 2026 on. Its ceiling-mounted camera has pointed at the ceiling tiles since the EFSF migration, so remote participants such as Legal see nothing. It is fixed by 28 May 2026.
